name: Miso Pork & Chicken Broth
description: A hearty pork-and-chicken base blended with red and white miso, finished with stir-fried garlic and ginger.

name: Tonkotsu (Pork Bone) Broth
description: Pork bones boiled hard and long until marrow and collagen emulsify into a cloudy, milky-white broth.

name: Clear Shoyu Broth
description: A clear, light-brown chicken-and-pork broth with a dashi component, seasoned with soy-sauce tare.

name: Clear Shio Broth
description: A delicate, clear broth from chicken, pork, and often seafood or kombu, seasoned only with salt.

name: Light Niboshi Shoyu Broth
description: A light pork-and-dried-sardine broth seasoned with shoyu, kept simple so the noodle stays the centerpiece.

name: Tonkotsu-Shoyu Hybrid Broth
description: A thick pork-bone broth blended directly with soy-sauce tare into one unified, heavy broth.

name: Double Soup Shoyu Broth
description: A pork-and-chicken bone base combined with a separate seafood dashi, seasoned with shoyu.

name: Tonkotsu-Chicken Hybrid Broth
description: A pork-bone tonkotsu base blended with chicken stock for a milder, rounder aroma than straight tonkotsu.

name: Miso Tare
description: A blend of red and white miso, sometimes with a touch of doubanjiang for gentle heat.

name: Shio Tare
description: A salt-based seasoning base, sometimes lifted with a little sake or light seafood seasoning.

name: Shoyu Tare
description: A soy-sauce base, typically blended with mirin, sake, or a small amount of sugar for balance.

name: Garlic-Ginger Fat
description: Garlic and ginger stir-fried into lard or vegetable oil before the broth is added.

name: Rendered Pork Fat
description: A simple rendered pork fat, sometimes with a garlic-oil addition, floated on the broth.

name: Insulating Lard Layer
description: A thin surface layer of lard or vegetable oil, floated specifically to keep the broth hot longer.

name: Black Garlic Oil (Mayu)
description: Fried garlic chips and toasted black garlic oil, stirred in just before serving for a nutty aroma.

name: No Aroma Oil (Clear Style)
description: No floated oil at all -- left off deliberately so a clear broth's own delicacy stays the focus.

name: Thick, Curly Egg Noodles
description: A springy, chewy egg-based noodle with enough structure to carry a thick broth without going limp.

name: Thin, Straight Noodles
description: A thin, low-hydration noodle designed to cook quickly -- light enough for a delicate broth or a kaedama refill.

name: Medium, Curly Noodles
description: A springy, moderate-hydration noodle that holds its bite without overwhelming a lighter broth.

name: Thick, Flat, Wavy Noodles
description: A distinctively thick, high-hydration noodle with a loose curl -- the defining feature of the bowl it's drawn from.

name: Thick, Straight, Flat Noodles
description: A dense, chewy, udon-adjacent noodle built to stand up to a heavy broth's full weight.

name: Medium-Thick, Straight Noodles
description: A noodle slightly thicker than a delicate style, able to carry extra aroma oil without disappearing.

name: Chashu (Pork Belly)
description: Braised or roasted pork belly, sliced thin -- ramen's most common protein topping.

name: Ground Pork
description: Seasoned ground pork, often stir-fried with the aroma oil's aromatics before the broth is added.

name: Bean Sprouts
description: Fresh, crisp bean sprouts -- a near-universal lightening element on rich Hokkaido bowls.

name: Sweet Corn
description: Sweet corn kernels, a signature Sapporo miso addition that softens the broth's intensity.

name: Spinach
description: Lightly blanched spinach, adding color and a clean, mineral note against a heavy broth.

name: Menma (Fermented Bamboo Shoots)
description: Fermented, seasoned bamboo shoots with a distinctive savory tang and crunch.

name: Ajitama (Marinated Egg)
description: A soft-boiled egg marinated in a soy-based liquid until the yolk turns a deep, jammy amber.

name: Nori (Dried Seaweed)
description: A sheet of dried seaweed propped against the bowl's edge, meant to be dipped rather than left to soak.

name: Naruto (Fish Cake)
description: A pink-swirled fish cake slice, mostly decorative but a traditional marker of a classic shoyu bowl.

name: Beni Shoga (Pickled Ginger)
description: Thin strands of sharp, vinegar-pickled red ginger, cutting through a rich Kyushu-style bowl.

name: Sesame Seeds
description: Toasted sesame seeds scattered on top for a light nutty accent.

name: Wood Ear Mushroom (Kikurage)
description: Thin strips of wood ear mushroom, prized for their crunchy, almost cartilage-like texture.

name: Fried Garlic Chips
description: Crisp fried garlic chips, echoing the black garlic oil finish underneath.

name: Butter Pat
description: A pat of butter melted in tableside, deepening an already-rich broth.

name: Lemon Slice
description: A thin lemon slice, brightening an already-delicate, clear broth.

name: No Finishing Touch (Clean)
description: No finishing addition -- the bowl is meant to be enjoyed exactly as built.
